title: Messaging & Streaming
summary: How services talk without waiting on each other — a durable buffer between sender and receiver that decouples them in time, load, and failure.

blocks.markdown:
Async messaging lets a sender hand off work and move on, instead of blocking on a reply.

- A **broker** stores the message durably; the receiver reads it later, independently.
- This **decouples** services in time, load, and failure — one slow service no longer freezes its callers.
- A burst becomes a growing **backlog** instead of dropped traffic.
- Fan-out becomes "publish once, N consumers subscribe" — adding a consumer touches no one else.

blocks.subTitle: What to reach for
blocks.markdown:
Match the tool to the shape of your data.

| Situation | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Event stream, replay, many readers | Log (Kafka) |
| Task queue, rich routing, RPC | Broker (RabbitMQ, SQS) |
| Order matters per key | Partition by that key |
| Must not lose a message | At-least-once + idempotent consumer |

blocks.subTitle: Queue vs log
blocks.markdown:
Two broker designs — confusing them drives most bad architecture calls.

![Queue versus append-only log](assets/messaging-streaming/queue-vs-log.svg)

- **Queue** — a message is a task done once. The broker deletes it on ack; many consumers split the work. This is RabbitMQ / SQS.
- **Log** — an immutable, ordered sequence kept for a retention window. Reading deletes nothing; each consumer tracks its own **offset** and can replay. This is Kafka / Kinesis.

blocks.subTitle: Kafka building blocks
blocks.markdown:
Kafka is the log model at scale — the system interviewers ask about most.

![Kafka topic partitions with a consumer group](assets/messaging-streaming/kafka-partitions-consumer-group.svg)

- **Topic** — a named stream, split into **partitions** (independent append-only logs).
- **Offset** — a message's position within one partition, unique there only.
- **Consumer group** — each partition is owned by exactly one consumer in the group; two groups each get the full stream.
- Same key → same partition (`hash(key) % N`), so a key's messages stay ordered.

assets.alt: Kafka topic partitions with a consumer group

blocks.subTitle: Replication & acks
blocks.markdown:
Each partition is copied to R brokers so a dead broker doesn't lose data.

- One replica is the **leader** (all reads/writes); followers copy it. The caught-up set is the **ISR**.
- If the leader dies, a follower from the ISR is promoted — no loss if it had the data.
- Producers pick durability via `acks`: `0` fire-and-forget, `1` leader-only, `all` every ISR has it.
- For "must not lose," use `acks=all` with `min.insync.replicas=2`. See [consistency-replication](consistency-replication).

blocks.subTitle: Delivery semantics
blocks.markdown:
It comes down to the order of two steps: doing the work and committing your offset.

![At-least-once with idempotent consumer flow](assets/messaging-streaming/delivery-semantics.svg)

- **At-most-once** — commit first, then process. A crash loses the message. No duplicates, possible loss.
- **At-least-once** — process first, then commit. A crash redelivers. No loss, possible duplicates. **The sane default.**
- **Exactly-once** — never lost, never duplicated in effect. Built, not configured.

blocks.subTitle: Exactly-once = idempotent consumer
blocks.markdown:
True exactly-once *delivery* over a network is impossible. You engineer exactly-once *effect*.

```python
def on_message(msg):       # msg.id is a stable unique id
    with db.transaction():
        if db.exists("charges", id=msg.id):
            commit_offset(msg)   # already done, no-op
            return
        pay.charge(msg.amount, key=msg.id)
        db.insert("charges", id=msg.id)  # unique constraint
    commit_offset(msg)               # only now: at-least-once
```

- The **unique constraint** plus one transaction make a redelivery a harmless no-op.
- Commit the offset **last**; a crash before it just replays into a no-op.

blocks.subTitle: Ordering & backpressure
blocks.markdown:
Ordering and flow control are where naive designs break.

- **Ordering** is guaranteed only *within a partition* — never across. Key by entity for per-entity order.
- A thread pool or unbounded retries can reorder even inside a partition; bound `max.in.flight.requests`.
- **Backpressure** in a log: the backlog grows up to retention and shows as rising **consumer lag**; scale consumers.
- The cardinal sin is an unbounded in-memory buffer that OOMs the broker.

blocks.subTitle: Log vs queue
blocks.markdown:
Both move messages — they trade differently.

| Aspect | Log (Kafka) | Queue (RabbitMQ) |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | Event stream | Task once |
| Throughput | Very high | Moderate |
| Replay | Yes, by offset | No |
| Routing | Basic | Rich |

Logs win on volume and replay; smart queues win on per-message routing and control.

blocks.subTitle: Plain-English rules
blocks.markdown:
Pick by what you're actually trading.

- **Data is a stream**, many teams want it or you want replay → **log (Kafka)**.
- **Data is a task** with rich routing or RPC → **queue (RabbitMQ / SQS)**.
- **Order matters for a key** → partition by that key; never trust global order.
- **Can't lose a message** → at-least-once + idempotent consumer, `acks=all`.
- **DB and broker written together** → outbox pattern, not dual writes.

blocks.subTitle: Real systems
blocks.markdown:
The same mental model, different operational bets.

- **Kafka** — replicated commit log; consumer-tracked offsets plus sequential I/O give millions of msgs/sec. Modern Kafka swaps ZooKeeper for **KRaft** (built-in Raft).
- **RabbitMQ** — routing intelligence: exchanges, bindings, per-message ack, DLQ first-class. Lower throughput, no long replay.
- **AWS SQS/SNS** — fully managed; standard is at-least-once, FIFO adds strict order; SNS is fanout.
- **Kinesis** — managed Kafka cousin; partitions are **shards**.

blocks.subTitle: What to monitor
blocks.markdown:
Messaging is invisible until it isn't. Watch:

- **Consumer lag** (per partition and group) — the top metric; sustained growth near retention means you'll lose unread data.
- **Produce vs consume rate** — if in exceeds out for long, lag grows.
- **Under-replicated partitions / ISR shrink** — reduced durability, page-worthy.
- **DLQ depth** — a growing DLQ means systematic failures.
- **Rebalance frequency** — frequent stop-the-world rebalances are a smell.

The mistakes that bite in interviews and production:

- **"Kafka gives exactly-once."** Only Kafka-to-Kafka; external side effects still need an idempotency key.
- **"Messages are globally ordered."** Only within a partition. Key by the entity whose order matters.
- **"More consumers means faster."** Capped at partition count; extras idle. Add partitions instead.
- **"Auto-commit is fine."** It can commit before work finishes, silently becoming at-most-once.
- **"I'll dual-write DB and broker."** Not atomic — use the outbox ([event-driven-cqrs](event-driven-cqrs)).
- **"Infinite retries fix flaky downstreams."** A poison message blocks the partition; cap retries plus DLQ.
